svg.text: Each panel is a Fourier transform of the same water levels, sampled differently. Read hourly, the tide's lines sit at 1.93 cpd (M2) and 1.0 cpd (K1). Every 6 hours (Nyquist 2 cpd)
they still sit there. Every 11, 24 or 25 hours they are above Nyquist (grey rule at the panel's right end) and reappear at |f − k·fs|, exactly where the dashed theory lines say: M2 at
0.068 cpd (14.8 days) for daily readings, K1 at 0.043 cpd (23 days) for 25-hourly ones (the table lists every peak against theory). K1 and S2 almost vanish into a constant, since daily
sampling sees them at nearly the same phase every time. Daily means (bottom) remove the tide instead of folding it.
